headline: Project-exit charges swamp a strong underlying quarter

kpis.label: Net income (loss) attributable to Air Products

summary_short: Air Products' Q3 FY2026 sales rose 5% y/y to $3.16B, but a $2.9B pre-tax project-exit charge drove a GAAP operating loss of $2.1B and a $6.47 diluted loss per share. Adjusted EPS, excluding the charge, rose 12% to $3.47; full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $13.39-$13.49.
summary_long: GAAP results were swamped by a $2,907.4M pre-tax ($9.92/share) charge tied to June 30, 2026 project-exit decisions -- abandoning the Louisiana Clean Energy Complex and the Casa Grande, Arizona hydrogen facility -- driving a $2,097.1M operating loss and $1,440.8M net loss. Excluding the charge, adjusted operating income rose 9% to $810.3M and adjusted EPS rose 12% to $3.47 on higher on-site volumes, pricing, favorable currency, and higher equity-affiliate income from Saudi Arabia. Nine-month capex fell 34% to $2,646.2M on lower NGHC-funded spending and the project exits. Cash fell to $980.5M after $3.35B of capex and $1.2B of dividends over nine months. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $13.39-$13.49; Q4 guidance set at $3.55-$3.65; FY26 capex now seen at ~$3.5B.

drivers.explanation: Three percent higher volumes, one percent higher pricing, and one percent favorable currency, led by Americas HyCO/on-site growth and higher Asia on-site and helium volumes.
Higher on-site volumes, favorable currency, and higher pricing, partially offset by higher costs.
Swamped by a $2,907.4M pre-tax charge for project-exit decisions announced June 30, 2026, including the Louisiana Clean Energy Complex and Casa Grande, Arizona hydrogen facility exits.

Reflects the June 30, 2026 decision to exit the Louisiana Clean Energy Complex and discontinue the Casa Grande zero-carbon liquid hydrogen facility plus other smaller clean-energy distribution projects.
Driven almost entirely by the project-exit charge, which alone cut EPS by $9.92 per share; excluding it, EPS rose.
Higher adjusted operating income plus higher equity affiliates' income, primarily from Saudi Arabia affiliates.

drivers.metric: Net income (loss) attributable to Air Products
drivers.explanation: Same project-exit charge drove the swing to a GAAP net loss from a year-ago profit.
Nine-month capex of $3.35B and $1.2B of dividends paid exceeded $3.31B of operating cash flow.
Lower NGHC-funded (non-recourse) project spending and reduced outlays following the June 30 project-portfolio exits.
Raised on continued adjusted EPS outperformance and expected benefits from new asset contributions, pricing actions, and productivity initiatives.

CEO Eduardo Menezes cited 12% adjusted EPS growth and high-single-digit adjusted operating income growth despite macro volatility, framing the GAAP loss as a portfolio-discipline decision rather than a core-business problem.
